name: Pain gating and endogenous opioid release (TENS-like coding)
driver_note: Rodent TENS: 100 Hz acts through spinal delta-opioid receptors and lowers spinal glutamate/aspartate; 4 Hz through mu-opioid receptors; alternating 2/100 Hz is more potent. These data are suprathreshold electrical stimulation; no retrieved paper shows opioid release from magnetic fields below peripheral nerve threshold.

windows.tolerance: daily TENS shows tolerance by day 4, prevented by NMDA blockade (Hingne 2007)

confidence: moderate in rodents, low for transfer to PEMF
caveat: 10-20 Hz was not tested in these papers. The 50-100 Hz acute and 10-20 Hz recovery assignment therefore rests on the 100 Hz vs 4 Hz TENS code, not on magnetic data.

name: Repetitive peripheral magnetic stimulation (rPMS) for pain and spasticity
driver_note: Intensity is set relative to motor threshold (120 % MT; 20-55 % MSO), so these devices work at or above peripheral motor threshold. Frequency 5-20 Hz, 10-20 min, 3,900-4,800 pulses per session.

windows.effect_duration: about 1 week after one session; none beyond 1-3 months in meta-analyses
windows.trial_effects: neuropathic pain NRS -1.64 (0-1 month, Dana 2023); fibromyalgia -1.86 (1-3 months, Leenus 2025); MSK SMD -1.16 (Pan 2025)

evidence: human RCTs and meta-analyses, low to very low GRADE
caveat: Short-lived effects; high heterogeneity (I2 up to 94 %).

name: Low-intensity PEMF for pain (clinical dose evidence)
driver_note: No trial reports dB/dt or induced E. B values are device settings and not measured at the target. Effects do not scale with B or dB/dt across studies.

windows.computed_E_Vm: 0.03-0.24 V/m for 2-10 mT, 50 Hz sine, r=0.10-0.15 m (computed, sinusoid assumption)
windows.meta: neuropathic pain SMD -1.01 but I2=92.8 % and gone after trim-and-fill; peripheral neuropathy -0.38 (-0.86 to 0.10) n.s. (Lara-Reyes 2026)

caveat: Only the 10 mT, 50 Hz arm (1 of 5) showed benefit in Taradaj 2018. Elshiwi 2018 pain CI crosses zero.

name: Subthreshold neuromodulation (LFMS, low-field transcranial)
driver: E amplitude with tissue-specific frequency tuning
driver_note: LFMS delivers about 0.7-1 V/m at 1 kHz, a few-fold below the SD-law PNS threshold at that frequency. Efficacy evidence is weak.
caveat: Mood improvement only in the pooled secondary analysis (Rohan 2014). Dufor 2019 argues pattern and cryptochrome rather than induced currents.

name: Nerve regeneration: direct DC electric field (in vitro window)
driver_note: Direct DC E of 20-100 V/m (10-100 mV/mm) increases DRG neurite outgrowth; >= 100 mV/mm or > 10 h at 10-30 mV/mm is toxic.
caveat: These are 4-5 orders of magnitude above the E a coil induces at 0.03-3 mT (0.1-10 mV/m, Walker 2007). They define the electrical window, not a PEMF threshold.

name: Nerve regeneration with low-B PEMF (rodent)
driver_note: Sisken-type effects (0.3 mT, 2 Hz, 4 h/day days 1-5) cannot be explained by E amplitude. Amplitude window is narrow (0.3 mT effective, 0.06 mT not). Repeated nulls at the same 0.3 mT.
caveat: PEMF lowered NGF in injured nerve (Longo 1999) and depressed NGF-driven neurite growth (Shah 2001); BDNF rose in other work. Direction is inconsistent.
